text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PAGER-1234 fired: SEV=high — gpu-node-42 reporting kubelet_not_ready. link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PAGER-1234 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Alert assigned to oncall: Maya (primary). Escalation policy will notify SRE lead if not acked in 2m.

Maya: acked. I'm on it — pulling node status now.

Maya: kubectl snapshot:
```
$ kubectl get nodes gpu-node-42 -o wide
NAME         STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    OS-IMAGE
gpu-node-42  NotReady  gpu     72d   v1.27.3   10.10.42.7     Ubuntu 22.04
```

Carlos: NotReady + kubelet not responding usually means kubelet crashed or disk/oom/dkms issue. Can you SSH and check kubelet/systemd logs?

Maya: SSHing to host.
```
$ ssh root@gpu-node-42
# journalctl -u kubelet --since "5m" --no-pager | tail -n 50
Mar 14 02:03:10 kubelet[1234]: E0324 02:03:10.123456   1234 kubelet.go:XXXX] Failed to get cgroup stats: cgroup not found
Mar 14 02:03:11 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 14 02:03:11 kernel: kernel: [  123.456789] possible DEQUEUE_LOCK or GPU reset
```

Priya: hmm gpu driver errors in dmesg. If GPU driver died, pod-level restarts might be spiking. We should cordon and drain this node to limit impact.

Maya: Attempting kubelet restart first:
```
$ systemctl restart kubelet
# systemctl status kubelet -n 5
● kubelet.service - kubelet: Failed
Mar 14 02:04:20 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```

Maya: restart failed — kubelet immediately OOM/killed. Ok proceeding to cordon + drain.

Maya: cordon + drain commands:
```
$ kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
node/gpu-node-42 cordoned
$ kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m
```

infra-bot: cordon job started (job-id: cj-2251). Drain in progress — migrating 12 pods: model-serving/redis-cache/sidecars.

Carlos: Good. Also notify runtime autoscaler to warm fallback capacity: @infra-bot can you spin up one reserved slot in rack-09 as warm spare?

infra-bot: warm spare request accepted, creating instance: gpu-warm-09-1. ETA ~90s.

Priya: Routing config updated to failover route for model-serving -> remove gpu-node-42 from LB. This will cause ~3m of 503s as in-flight requests drain.

Maya: Drain completed successfully. Output:
```
evicted pod/model-serving-abc123 -> rescheduled on gpu-node-33
evicted pod/redis-cache-12345 -> rescheduled on gpu-node-11
All pods evicted
```

Maya: Checking customer impact now — metrics show a spike in 503s for inference-api between 02:03:00-02:06:00. Approx 142 failed requests, 90th latency spike.

Marcus: Marcus (SRE Lead) joining. Thanks for the quick actions. Given dmesg indicates GPU dropped off PCI bus, I approve host reboot to attempt hardware reinitialization. Coordinate timing — avoid simultaneous reboots in the same rack.

Maya: Roger. Initiating reboot now.
```
$ sudo reboot now
Connection to gpu-node-42 closed by remote host.
```

pagerduty-bot: PAGER-1234 status updated: acknowledged by Maya, escalated to Marcus for approval, action: reboot initiated.

Carlos: While node reboots, let's gather kernel oops for postmortem. Maya, can you dump dmesg and nvme logs after it comes back?

Maya: Will capture on boot and upload to S3 path s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2251234000/gpu-node-42/. I'll also run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` if driver comes up.

[~90s later]

infra-bot: Host gpu-node-42 is back online, boot time 110s. Node shows NotReady for a minute while kubelet re-registers.

Maya: kubectl get nodes shows rejoined but kubelet still NotReady initially:
```
$ kubectl get nodes gpu-node-42 -o wide
NAME         STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-42  NotReady   gpu      72d   v1.27.3
```

Maya: systemctl status kubelet now shows it running. Checking Kubelet logs.
```
Apr 14 02:06:30 kubelet[1234]: Node registered with kube-apiserver
Apr 14 02:06:35 kubelet[1234]: Successfully registered node event: NodeReady
```

Maya: Node transitioned to Ready. `kubectl get nodes` now shows Ready.

Maya: Post-reboot checks: nvidia-smi OK, driver loaded, nvme SMART OK. Uploading bugreport and dmesg excerpts.

infra-bot: Uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2251234000/dmesg.txt, bugreport.tar.gz.

Priya: Rolling a small canary of model-serving on gpu-node-42 to confirm stability.

Maya: Canary run looks good — inference latency stable, no driver errors so far. Will keep node cordoned for 10m of observation then uncordon.

Marcus: Good. Incident summary so far: cause likely transient GPU driver/hardware fault causing kernel to drop GPU from PCI bus -> kubelet OOM/killed -> node NotReady. Impact: ~142 failed requests across inference API for ~3 minutes. No customer data lost. Action items: 1) follow up with hardware vendor for PCI/GPU investigation (assigned Carlos), 2) add kernel oops alert to incident rule (Priya), 3) playbook update: run nvidia-bug-report automatically on reboot (Maya).

Maya: Uncordoning node now.
```
$ kubectl uncordon gpu-node-42
node/gpu-node-42 uncordoned
```

Maya: All model-serving pods rescheduled and passed readiness probes.

oncall-rotation: Handoff note — Maya will be on-call for the next 2 hours; Marcus please follow for postmortem.

Marcus: I'll own the postmortem and vendor escalation. Please attach all logs to the incident ticket PD-4567.

Maya: Uploaded timeline and temp RCA to PD-4567. Closing the page now. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: PAGER-1234 resolved by Maya — reason: node rebooted and passed health checks.

Maya: Final notes to include in PM: limit concurrent workloads during hardware flaps, improve kubelet restart backoff handling, and add an automated warm-spare spin-up for GPU rack.

Carlos: I'll open a hardware RMA ticket with vendor and link the bugreport.

Priya: I'll add the alert rule and update runbook steps for this class of failures.

Maya: Thanks team.

incident-bot: Thread closed by Maya at ts=2251234680.
